outcome: Bleeding events (circumcision, soft tissue, oral, head injury)
cohort: The study included 547 babies aged ≤2 years with haemophilia who were enrolled in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Universal Data Collection System surveillance project at US Hemophilia Treatment Centers.
finding: Bleeding events were common in haemophilic babies ≤2 years, with inhibitors significantly increasing rates of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) and central venous access device (CVAD) complications.
mod_finding: No detectable difference in the rates of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) by the mode of delivery was noted.
